title: Identity Basics: IAM, Principals, and Service Accounts — Failure Injection & Auto-Healing
purpose: Simulates service account credential failure: demonstrates expired OAuth tokens and IAM role revocation triggering immediate 403 Forbidden rejections.
routing_rationale: When IAM permissions are revoked in Cloud IAM, downstream API calls fail instantaneously across Google's globally synchronized policy cache.

nodes.label: Attacker / Hijacked Pod
nodes.detail: Malicious payload attempting to exfiltrate customer records via service account.

nodes.label: Local Token Cache
nodes.detail: Holds active OAuth bearer token issued prior to incident declaration.

nodes.label: SecOps Incident Responder
nodes.detail: Revokes roles/storage.admin binding and disables Service Account immediately.

nodes.label: Google Global Policy Cache
nodes.detail: Propagates permission revocation globally within 15 seconds; returns 403 Forbidden.

steps.title: Emergency Revocation
steps.action: Security team strips all IAM roles from service account via gcloud iam.
steps.why_traversal: Disabling the parent service account invalidates active bearer tokens globally.

steps.title: Exfiltration Blocked
steps.action: Compromised pod sends GET request with bearer token to Cloud Storage.
steps.why_traversal: Every Google Cloud API call verifies IAM bindings at runtime.

steps.title: Instant Lockdown
steps.action: Google policy cache rejects token with HTTP 403 Forbidden; exfiltration halted.
steps.why_traversal: Global synchronization halts compromised session within seconds without VM reboot.

scenarios.label: Unauthorized IAM Role Escalation Attempt
scenarios.root_cause: Attacker exploited container vulnerability to call iam.serviceAccounts.setIamPolicy.
scenarios.blast_radius: Confined to compromised container; cluster permissions unmodified.
scenarios.recovery: Isolate compromised pod; patch container base image and rotate secrets.
